ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point E is a point on the extension line of side BC of square ABCD, and $CE=BD$. AE intersects DC at point F. What is the measure of $\angle AFC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct line AC,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
thus AC=BD,\\
since CE=BD,\\
thus CE=AC,\\
thus $\angle$E=$\angle$CAE,\\
since AC is the diagonal of square ABCD,\\
thus $\angle$ACB=$45^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$E+$\angle$CAE=$45^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$E=$ \frac{1}{2} \times 45^\circ=22.5^\circ$,\\
In $\triangle$CEF, $\angle$AFC=$\angle$E+$\angle$ECF=$22.5^\circ+90^\circ=\boxed{112.5^\circ}$.

Since B,C,E are collinear and CE is the opposite extension of CB, the interior angle at C in triangle ACE is ∠ACE = 180° - 45° = 135°. Therefore the sum of the two base angles is 180° - 135° = 45°, and the two are equal, so ∠CEA = ∠CAE = 22.5°. In triangle CEF, CF is on the square side DC, and CE is on the extension of BC, therefore CF ⟂ CE, ∠ECF = 90°. Also E,F,A are collinear, so ∠CEF = ∠CEA = 22.5°. ∠AFC is the exterior angle at point F of triangle CEF, equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, that is, ∠AFC = ∠CEF + ∠ECF = 22.5° + 90° = 112.5°.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Construct line AC. Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, AC = BD. Since CE = BD, CE = AC. Thus \angle E = \angle CAE. Since AC is the diagonal of square ABCD, \angle ACB = 45^\circ. Thus \angle E + \angle CAE = 45^\circ, so \angle E = \frac{1}{2} \times 45^\circ = 22.5^\circ. In \triangle CEF, \angle AFC = \angle E + \angle ECF = 22.5^\circ + 90^\circ = \boxed{112.5^\circ}.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; BC is extended rightward to point E. Segment AE goes obliquely downward to the right from A through the right side DC of the square, intersects DC at F, and continues to E. The diagonal BD of the square is also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: According to the method, draw auxiliary line AC. Because ABCD is a square, the two diagonals are equal, AC = BD. The problem statement gives CE = BD, therefore CE = AC. Thus in triangle ACE, AC = CE, it is an isosceles triangle with AE as the base, so ∠CAE = ∠CEA. Also because AC is the diagonal of the square, ∠ACB = 45°. Since B,C,E are collinear and CE is the opposite extension of CB, the interior angle at C in triangle ACE is ∠ACE = 180° - 45° = 135°. Therefore the sum of the two base angles is 180° - 135° = 45°, and the two are equal, so ∠CEA = ∠CAE = 22.5°. In triangle CEF, CF is on the square side DC, and CE is on the extension of BC, therefore CF ⟂ CE, ∠ECF = 90°. Also E,F,A are collinear, so ∠CEF = ∠CEA = 22.5°. ∠AFC is the exterior angle at point F of triangle CEF, equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, that is, ∠AFC = ∠CEF + ∠ECF = 22.5° + 90° = 112.5°.
